source_text: Neque enim deesse cottidianus cibus potest iusto, cum scriptumsit: non occidet Dominus fame animam iustam, et iterum: iuuenior fui et senui et non uidi iustum derelictum neque semen eius quaerens panem, item Dominus promittat et dicat: nolite cogitare dicentes: quid edemus aut quid bibemus aut quid uestiemur? haec enim nationes quaerunt. scit autem pater uester quia horum omnium indigetis. quaerite primo regnum et iustitiam Dei, et haec omnia adponentur uobis. quaerentibus regnum et iustitiam Dei omnia promittit adponi. nam cum Dei sint omnia, habenti Deum nihil deerit, si Deo ipse non desit. sic Danieli in leonum lacum iussu regis incluso prandium diuinitus procuratur et inter feras esurientes et parcentes homo Dei pascitur. sic alitur Helias in fuga et solitudine coruis ministrantibus et uolucribus cibum sibi adportantibus in persecutione nutritur. adque — o humanae malitiae detestanda crudelitas ! – ferae parcunt, aues pascunt, et homines insidiantur et saeuiunt!
thought_title: God feeds the just and the wicked starve them
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the petition for daily bread, arguing that God supplies all things to those who seek his kingdom and justice.
pass_a_gloss: Neither [and] for [it] can be lacking daily food to the just [man], since [it] has been written: [he] will not kill [the] Lord by hunger [the] just soul, and again: younger I was and I grew old and not I have seen [the] just [man] forsaken nor his seed seeking bread, likewise [the] Lord may promise and may say: do not think saying: what will we eat or what will we drink or what will we be clothed with? these things for [the] nations seek. [he] knows but your father that of all these [things] you have need. seek first [the] kingdom and [the] justice of God, and these all [things] will be added to you. to [those] seeking [the] kingdom and [the] justice of God all [things] [he] promises to be added. for since of God are all [things], [to him] having God nothing will be lacking, if to God he himself not should be lacking. so to Daniel into [the] lions' pit by [the] command of [the] king shut in [a] meal divinely is provided and among [the] beasts hungering and sparing [him] [the] man of God is fed. so is fed Elijah in flight and solitude [with] ravens ministering and birds food to him bringing in persecution [he] is nourished. and – o of human malice detestable cruelty! – [the] beasts spare, [the] birds feed, and [the] men lie in wait and rage!

choices.term: non occidet Dominus fame animam iustam
choices.english: the Lord will not kill the soul of the just man by hunger
choices.why: Literal rendering of the Old Latin wording; 'animam iustam' is kept as 'soul of the just man' to preserve the biblical idiom
rejected: the Lord will not let the righteous go hungry

choices.term: quaerite primo regnum et iustitiam Dei
choices.english: seek first the kingdom and the justice of God
choices.why: Literal word order and 'justice' for 'iustitiam' to match Cyprian's Latin rather than modern 'righteousness'
rejected: seek first God's kingdom and righteousness

choices.term: habenti Deum nihil deerit, si Deo ipse non desit
choices.english: nothing will be lacking to the one who has God, if he himself does not fail God
choices.why: Preserves the wordplay between 'deerit' and 'desit' and the dative construction
rejected: whoever has God will lack nothing, if he does not abandon God

choices.english: O detestable cruelty of human malice
choices.why: Keeps the exclamatory force and the genitive phrase literally
rejected: how detestable is the cruelty of human wickedness

choices.term: ferae parcunt, aues pascunt, et homines insidiantur et saeuiunt
choices.english: wild beasts spare, birds feed, and men plot against and rage
choices.why: Preserves the stark parallel structure and the present tense verbs
rejected: wild animals spare them, birds feed them, while men attack and rage

pass_b_english: Daily bread cannot be lacking to the just man, since it is written: the Lord will not kill the soul of the just man by hunger (Proverbs 10:3), and again: I was young and I have grown old, and I have not seen the just man forsaken, nor his seed seeking bread (Psalm 37:25 (Psalm 36:25 in the Septuagint)). Likewise the Lord promises and says: Do not be anxious, saying, What shall we eat, or what shall we drink, or what shall we wear? For the nations seek all these things. But your Father knows that you need all these things. Seek first the kingdom and the justice of God, and all these things will be added to you (Matthew 6:31-33). To those who seek the kingdom and the justice of God, he promises that all things will be added. For since all things belong to God, nothing will be lacking to the one who has God, if he himself does not fail God. So Daniel, shut in the lions' den by the king's command, is provided a meal from heaven, and among hungry beasts that spare him the man of God is fed. So Elijah is nourished in flight and solitude, with ravens serving him and birds bringing him food in persecution. And—O detestable cruelty of human malice!—wild beasts spare, birds feed, and men plot against and rage!

last_rejected.quote: the Lord will not kill the soul of the just man by hunger
last_rejected.source_quote: non occidet Dominus fame animam iustam
last_rejected.why: "occidet" means "slay/destroy by death," not "kill by hunger"; "fame" is ablative of means ("by hunger"), but the sense is "the Lord will not let the just soul die of hunger/starvation," not actively "kill."
last_rejected.fix: the Lord will not slay the just soul by hunger
last_rejected.ruling: occidet + ablative fame = 'kill by hunger'; 'kill by hunger' accurately renders the Latin.

last_rejected.why: "quaerens" is nominative singular agreeing with "semen" (his seed), not a participle describing an action; the meaning is "nor his seed begging/seeking bread" i.e., reduced to begging.
last_rejected.fix: nor his seed begging for bread
last_rejected.ruling: quaerens is nominative agreeing with semen; 'seeking bread' correctly renders it.

last_rejected.quote: Likewise the Lord promises and says
last_rejected.why: The subjunctive "promittat...dicat" indicates this is a quotation of Christ's words (as marked in voices), but the English flattens this to a simple statement, losing the hortatory/quotative force and the speaker identification.
last_rejected.fix: So too the Lord promises and says
last_rejected.ruling: promittat/dicat subjunctive in continuation of scriptural citation; 'promises and says' is adequate.

last_rejected.why: "cogitare" means "think/worry" but the Latin "dicentes" ("saying") is present; the Greek and standard translations have "do not worry/be anxious saying." However, "cogitare" is stronger than "be anxious"—it's "do not think/say" or "do not worry." The issue is "anxious" adds a nuance not in "cogitare."
last_rejected.ruling: cogitare includes 'be anxious'; standard rendering of this Vulgate passage.

last_rejected.quote: if he himself does not fail God
last_rejected.why: "desit" from "deesse" means "be lacking/absent/fail" but the construction "si Deo ipse non desit" means "if he himself is not lacking to God" i.e., "if he does not abandon God"; "fail God" is ambiguous and could mean "fail to serve God" which is close, but "is not lacking to God" or "does not abandon God" is clearer.
last_rejected.fix: if he himself does not fail to be found in God
last_rejected.ruling: 'fail God' is normal English for deesse + dative; meaning is clear.

last_rejected.quote: with ravens serving him and birds bringing him food
last_rejected.source_quote: coruis ministrantibus et uolucribus cibum sibi adportantibus
last_rejected.why: "coruis" are specifically ravens, and "uolucribus" are birds generally; but the Latin makes ravens and birds parallel (both bringing food), while English "ravens serving him and birds bringing him food" oddly distinguishes "serving" from "bringing food" as if different actions, and "birds" seems to add a second category when ravens are birds. The Latin has ravens ministering and birds carrying food—likely hendiadys or parallel description of the same ravens as birds.
last_rejected.fix: with ravens as his ministers, birds bringing him food
last_rejected.ruling: Latin has two ablative absolutes: coruis ministrantibus and uolucribus adportantibus; English renders both adequately.

last_rejected.why: "persecutione" here refers to Elijah's being persecuted/fleeing from persecution (Ahab/Jezebel), not "in persecution" as a state; "while persecuted" or "in his flight from persecution" is needed.
last_rejected.ruling: 'in persecutione' = 'in persecution'; literal rendering is accurate for the context.

last_rejected.why: "insidiantur" means "lie in ambush/set traps for" (with implied object, likely the just man/God's servant), and "saeuiunt" means "rage/are cruel"; "plot against" loses the specific ambush/entrapment sense, and the objects are missing—men lay traps for the just and rage against them.
last_rejected.fix: men lie in wait and rage
last_rejected.ruling: insidiantur = 'plot against/lie in ambush'; 'plot against' is within normal range.
